linkedin:4492139381.description:
About The Role
We’re looking for a scientist who treats a model as a product. You want to know who will rely on its output and what decision it supports before choosing an architecture, and you measure success by whether researchers trust and use the result, not by whether the model shipped.
At Bolt Insight, our platform helps product, marketing and research teams understand their customers through AI-moderated interviews, real-time chat, media analysis and research insights. The Simulation Suite is our next big step: AI Personas, Digital Twins and synthetic respondents that let teams explore consumer behaviour faster, at lower cost and at a scale real fieldwork can’t reach.
In market research, a synthetic respondent is only useful if the industry can trust it, so every release passes a methodology gate before it reaches customers. As Product Scientist, you decide what the Simulation Suite should become scientifically, and you build and validate it yourself. You’ll own the technical direction and roadmap together with Product, Research and Engineering, and spend most of your time hands-on with data and models.
What You’ll Be Doing
Build and prototype the models. Persona and twin construction, calibration against real survey and interview data, prompt and agent design, retrieval and evaluation pipelines. You’ll write and review code and pair with engineers on the path to production.
Define and run validation. Design the evidence we need to prove a twin or persona is good enough: benchmarks against ground-truth studies, distributional fidelity, consistency, bias and drift checks. Build our synthetic validation framework and an evidence pack aligned with ESOMAR and MRS guidance, and work with our methodology team to pass the release gate.
Own the Simulation Suite roadmap. Turn bets into clear, shippable increments: category-specific Digital Twins, the Digital Twins MVP for pilot clients, agentic quantitative segments, always-on synthetic panels and moderated focus groups, and eventually multi-category, self-serve twin creation. Prioritise, write crisp specs and keep the work moving.
Make the trade-offs explicit. Decide what is good enough for a pilot versus GA, and where synthetic data complements real fieldwork and where it shouldn’t replace it. Communicate those limits honestly to customers and internal teams.
Work with LLMs in production. Build on OpenAI, Claude and Gemini using LangChain and LangGraph, and evaluate with Langfuse. Balance quality, latency
